subject: [PATCH 05/22] mm/mempolicy: keep interleave and tmpfs mount policies on common memory

2026-11-14.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's memory policy to use a new set of common memory nodes (N_MEMORY_COMMON) instead of N_MEMORY for boot memory policy calculations and their per-node sysfs entries. It also restricts the node set applied by mpol_set_nodemask() and mbind() masks to N_MEMORY_COMMON nodes. This change is intended to simplify the management of memory policies and ensure that all memory is considered common at this point, with no immediate behavior changes.

reviews.author: Richard Cheng
reviews.summary: Reviewer Richard Cheng questioned whether it's assumed that all common memory nodes are online, potentially invalidating the patch's logic for restricting node sets.
reviews.raw_body:
Maybe I overlooked or somehow, but when do we have the assumption
that common memory is definitely onlined ?

Best regards,
Richard Cheng.

reviews.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the code's behavior at init time makes checking N_MEMORY_COMMON unnecessary and agreed that existing code could simply check N_MEMORY for the same result.
reviews.raw_body:
For this particular case it's not particularly relevant.

This code only runs at init time, so it's either got memory or it
doesn't.  If the memory is present but offline, it still wants weights.

There isn't really a bug here, but the existing code could also just
check N_MEMORY and end up with the same result.  If the memory is
hotplugged later, it still gets weights accordingly.

-- 
~Gregory

2026-11-18.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's memory policy code to use a new set of common memory nodes (N_MEMORY_COMMON) instead of N_MEMORY for boot memory policy calculations and their per-node sysfs entries. It also restricts the node set applied by mpol_set_nodemask() and mbind() masks to N_MEMORY_COMMON nodes, ensuring that only eligible nodes are considered for memory policies. This change is intended to simplify the code and improve performance, but does not introduce any immediate behavior changes since all memory is initially common.
